requirement_text.note: Verbatim descriptions: handoffs/ADHOC-20261005-001/step-01-code-designer.json context.requirement_text. This step reviews a decision record, not an implementation; scope the read to the ADR plus the security-relevant sources it cites.

source_text.coordinator_request: REVIEWER and SECURITY-REVIEWER must check the ADR's consistency with docs/migration/decisions/ especially 0002, 0006, 0035, 0038, 0042, 0043 and security-invariants INV-1..INV-8.

task.description: SECURITY gate on the PROPOSED decision record docs/migration/decisions/0044-hybrid-identity-model.md (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS after 1 rework). It proposes a possible future shared-tier identity model (central realm, tenant selector, membership authorisation, domain-based routing) and a rollout whose Phase 1 is the already-ratified email-first directory. Review as a security design review: (a) the tenant-selector + membership rule and the INV-5 equivalence class (ADR 2.3.5): can a caller with a shared-realm account reach, read or be provisioned into a tenant they are not a member of; is 'JIT off for the shared realm' sufficient; what else could confer cross-tenant access (token claims, group/role mapping, subject collisions, email-verified/unverified emails, account linking, org membership vs local users row, deactivation propagation, token refresh)? (b) the weakening of 0006 s3.2 / R5 claims and 0002 'sole source' sentence: are the amendments honestly stated and bounded? (c) domain-based routing inference (R-7) and enumeration posture vs INV-5 and 0042 standing prohibitions (do the O3 additions keep the discovery response closed and byte-uniform?); (d) INV-1..INV-9 mapping in 2.3.7 and 6.7: is each correct against security-invariants.md (read the invariants file; quote the text you rely on); (e) anything the ADR should say but does not (e.g. account takeover via email change in the central realm, org-admin delegation, break-glass, audit trail per tenant, token audience/issuer pinning, logout/session scope, mobile token storage). Verify claims about this repo by reading the cited files (auth_pipeline.ex, identity.ex etc.). Do NOT edit the ADR. Output verdict RATIFIED/PASS or FAIL with findings classified BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/ADVICE and exact locations; a FAIL means ORCH routes rework to CODE-DESIGNER. Note the ADR is PROPOSED and the user ratifies; your verdict is about security soundness and honesty of the record, not about choosing the option. Write the result into this handoff's 'result' (status PASS/FAIL, summary, issues[]) and set status COMPLETED; do not spawn agents; do not commit.
acceptance_criteria: INV-1..INV-9 mapping verified against security-invariants.md text

result.summary: SECURITY-REVIEWER re-review of 0044 after rework 2 (commit 3ea301b8): PASS. 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR, 4 MINOR, 1 ADVICE. All of SR-1..SR-9 are resolved in the text and SR-10 is carried as 2.3.9; the previous FAIL drivers (domain routing vs 0042 prohibitions, 0006 s3.2 downgrade, fail-open JIT default, realm disjointness, INV-5 ordering/decoy/collapsed response, invitation security) are now stated correctly and bounded. Coherence check: 'never a 200 in Mode A / uniform tenant' plus 'one joined constant-work query' is consistent with 0042 prohibitions 6, 7, 11 (6.5 correctly lists them as AMENDS for Phase 4) and with 0043 D-A (200 only for exactly one active match with disclose true; uniform tenant byte-identical to unknown); the only gap is that the named residual oracle is understated (N-1). Quotes verified against sources (14 checked, all match modulo em-dash rendering and ellipses): 0002:168-171 (sole source of truth) and 190-195 (one shared host, N realms, bare realm slug); 0035:39-42 (Keycloak-hosted-only login is the correct, working, intended production architecture) and 15-17 (no /login route; file is 0035-frontend-login-delegated-to-keycloak.md); 0038:65-75, 76-81 (point 4), 100-103 (no automatic/JIT membership rows); 0043:229-233 (D-G deferred) and 187-192 (D-E); 0042:111-114 (scope fence), 160-163 (what remains unchanged); 0006:296-297 (7.3), 188-195, 303-306. INV-1..INV-9 mapping in 2.1, 2.3.7, 6.7 re-checked against security-invariants.md: correct. The remaining MINORs are wording/scope fixes that Phase 2 acceptance can absorb; none changes the soundness of the proposal. Not a verdict on choosing O1/O2/O3.

previous_findings_status.SR-1: RESOLVED: 2.3.2 item 3 now forbids a second-lookup fallback (one joined constant-work query, or not at discovery), never a 200 in Mode A / uniform tenant; 6.5 lists AMENDS for prohibitions 6, 7, 11 and narrows CONSISTENT to 1-5, 8-10, 12-14 in Phases 1-3; R-7 and Phase 4 row updated. Coherent with 0043 D-A (200 only when exactly one active match AND disclose true; uniform tenants byte-identical to unknown). See N-1 for a residual understatement.
previous_findings_status.SR-2: RESOLVED: 2.3.4 and 6.2 call it a DOWNGRADE from DB constraint to application invariant, require one dedicated writer distinct from provision_oidc_user/4, refusal in create_user/2 and update_user_profile/3 (both exist, identity.ex:227, 337) and a DB backstop or explicit statement. Minor wording residual N-4.
previous_findings_status.SR-3: RESOLVED: 2.3.5 4a (structural branch, never calls provision_oidc_user/sync_role_claims_from_token) and 4b (fail-open default documented with accurate citations, absent-realm test as Phase 2 acceptance). Residual N-2.
previous_findings_status.SR-4: RESOLVED: 2.3.4 rules (i) disjointness (changeset, creation, trigger or boot assertion) and (ii) realm kind decided once before resolve_tenant; S-11 and Phase 2 row carry them.
previous_findings_status.SR-5: RESOLVED: 2.3.5 item 3 fixes ordering slug -> membership -> status, one collapsed byte-identical response (distinct current bodies named), decoy query for round-trip parity, Phase 2 tests for equal round trips and bytes. Advice N-5.
previous_findings_status.SR-6: RESOLVED: new 2.3.8 covers binding to (realm, sub), email_verified and address match, 128-bit hashed single-use expiring token, leak handling, rate limiting, collapsed response, single writer. Contradiction N-3 on path vs fragment.
previous_findings_status.SR-7: RESOLVED: 2.1 INV-9 wording now correct (no tenant-controlled outbound URL; notifier carries no tenant-derived URL).
previous_findings_status.SR-8: RESOLVED: S-11 now requires full issuer check and that a shared-realm token cannot satisfy a dedicated chain.

previous_findings_status.SR-10: RESOLVED as advice: 2.3.9 adds mutable email / no auto-link by email, break-glass, per-tenant audit, SSO/logout scope, mobile refresh token, directory never membership source.

issues.finding: The named residual says 'domain-level, not person-level'. Under form (a) it is not purely domain-level: at a routed domain a lone routed tenant gives 200 (disclosing tenant), but if the same address ALSO has a directory row in another tenant the match set is multi (0043 D-A: 200 only for exactly ONE active match), so the response is 202. 200 vs 202 therefore reveals, for any mailbox at that domain, whether it is registered in some other tenant. Also, for a uniform tenant a domain match would e-mail a tenant list to any local part at the domain, including mailboxes that do not exist (notifier amplification, bounded by the per-address and per-IP limits). Not a prohibition breach (the 0042 single-match inference is already accepted) but the record understates it.
issues.required: Restate the residual to include 'address also registered elsewhere' and the notifier behaviour for domain-only matches; require dedupe by tenant when the same tenant matches by directory and by domain; decide whether domain-only matches may trigger e-mail at all.

issues.finding: 4b says the unconfigured-realm fallback 'must become a typed deny' and requires a test. The ADR does not note that every existing dedicated realm other than bpm-default (QA: bilimbaga, swiftroute, meridian, vortex) is absent from the JIT map in config/prod.exs and dev.exs and today relies on the fail-open default. A global deny would block their first-time logins. The statement needs scope: either deny for realms classed shared (the shared branch never reads these maps per 4a), or an explicit prior step adding entries for all existing realms.
issues.required: State the scope and the ordering (populate explicit entries for existing realms, then flip the default).

issues.finding: The route is written `/invite/<opaque token>` (path) in 2.3.1/2.3.2/6.3, but 2.3.8 item 4 requires the token not to reach access logs and to be read from the URL fragment. A path segment is sent to the SPA host and appears in its access logs; only a fragment (`/invite#<token>`) does not. Internal contradiction.
issues.required: Change the route form to a fragment (or state the path form is logged-and-hashed and why acceptable) consistently.

issues.where: docs/migration/decisions/0044-hybrid-identity-model.md 2.3.4 replacement guarantee ('invitation or admin action created it'), 2.2 ('or equivalent'), Phase 5 / 2.2 migration (re-link by email)
issues.finding: The replacement guarantee still says rows exist only if 'an invitation or admin action created it', while (a)/(b) in the same bullet say exactly ONE writer (invitation acceptance) and create_user/2 must refuse shared realms. 2.2 keeps 'tenant-admin invitation or equivalent'. The Phase 5 re-link tool matches by email and rewrites external_realm/external_id, which would be a second writer of shared-realm rows and is account linking by e-mail, against 2.3.9 and 2.3.8 item 1.
issues.required: Reword the guarantee to 'only the invitation-acceptance writer'; drop 'or equivalent'; require Phase 5 re-link to be an operator tool bound to a verified (realm, sub) and to be listed as the sole exception to the single writer.

issues.finding: 'Fixed decoy target' is not defined. For parity the decoy must run the same query shape against a real tenant-schema users table with the same indexes, and the unknown-slug and non-member paths must also match in schema derivation and error construction cost; round-trip count alone is a weak proxy for timing.
issues.required: Define the decoy and add a coarse timing assertion to the Phase 2 tests, or accept round trips as the INV-5 standard (as security-invariants.md:199-204 words it).
